rationale:
Evidence: all eight designs so far ended off-track in all 60 trials per design. The off-track limit is 0.06 m for every body width in range, and max_error sits at 0.061 to 0.066 m whatever the gain, speed or sensor span. Progress is nearly fixed by track (oval about 0.12 to 0.17, s-bend about 0.04 to 0.07), so the robot fails at roughly the same early point each time. Iteration 7 (sensors at +/-0.03 m, 12 mm footprints, base 0.9, kp 1.6, kd 1.0) is the only design with a clear signal: it had 1 line-loss event per run instead of 2, and slalom progress rose from 0.06 to 0.11. Narrowing the span appears to reduce line losses, so I keep that geometry. Gain sweeps have not moved the failure point, so the untested factor I will change is speed, which has only been reduced to 0.8 at most.

Changes: (1) Geometry kept from iteration 7: seven sensors at x = -0.03 to +0.03 in 0.01 m steps, y = 0.06, 12 mm footprints, wheel_track 0.14, wheel_radius 0.03, mass 0.4, body unchanged. This isolates the controller change on the setup that showed fewer line losses. (2) base_speed reduced from 0.9 to 0.6, which gives the loop more time per bend and cuts lateral slip. The trade-off is that completion within 3 s is out of reach, so the aim is a stable run that covers more of the track. (3) kp reduced from 1.6 to 1.2, since a slower robot needs less steering gain to avoid overshoot. (4) ki kept at 0.3 to cancel the fixed motor-mismatch bias, with the integral bounded at +/-2. (5) kd reduced from 1.0 to 0.6 so the derivative term does not amplify the faster sensor transitions at the narrower span. (6) line_loss stays last_direction, because line loss is now less frequent and changing it is not justified by the evidence.

Expected result: fewer line-loss events (near 0 to 1 per run), max_error below about 0.05 m, and progress above 0.2 on the development tracks, with the slalom and s-bend improving most. Completion is unlikely. If max_error still reaches 0.06 at 0.6 base speed, the cause is probably not speed or gain, and the next draft should change wheel_track or wheel_radius.
